patient.chief_complaint: Progressive bilateral foot and leg weakness for 8 months following chemotherapy for multiple myeloma
patient.history_present_illness: Charles Fenwick is a 67-year-old retired professor presenting 8 months post-completion of bortezomib-based chemotherapy for IgG kappa multiple myeloma (achieved complete response). He reports progressive bilateral foot and leg weakness that began during his third cycle of bortezomib and has worsened despite completion of therapy 4 months ago. He has bilateral foot drop and significant difficulty climbing stairs. He also reports severe burning and shooting pain in both hands and feet that he rates 8/10, which interferes with sleep and activities of daily living. His oncologist attributed this to 'expected bortezomib peripheral neuropathy' and started gabapentin 600 mg three times daily with only partial pain relief. However, Charles notes that over the past 6 weeks he has experienced three episodes of sudden severe grip weakness in his right hand lasting 30-60 seconds followed by recovery, which he has not reported to his oncologist as he attributed them to fatigue. He also notes that his symptoms seem to fluctuate — some days much better than others. He has had a repeat serum protein electrophoresis at 2 months post-treatment showing complete response (no M-spike), but his light chain ratio was mildly abnormal at 3.2 (kappa 42 mg/L, lambda 13 mg/L). He denies bowel or bladder dysfunction. His ECOG performance status has deteriorated from 0 at diagnosis to 2 now.

Neuropathy Workup.value: No M-spike on SPEP — HOWEVER immunofixation: trace IgM kappa band detected

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Hemoglobin 11.4 g/dL (L), eGFR 58 mL/min/1.73m² (L), Serum Free Light Chain Kappa 42 mg/L (H), Kappa:Lambda Ratio 3.2 (H), HbA1c 7.4 % (H), Anti-MAG antibody POSITIVE — titer 1:12,800 (H), IgM paraprotein detected on immunofixation (trace IgM kappa band).
abnormal_values_summary: Serum Free Light Chain Kappa: 42 mg/L (H)

specialized_test.impression: ABNORMAL NCS/EMG — mixed demyelinating and axonal pattern. Distal motor latencies disproportionately prolonged relative to conduction velocity slowing (terminal slowing pattern) bilaterally in upper and lower limb nerves. Sensory nerve action potentials reduced or absent. Conduction velocities mildly slowed without significant conduction block. EMG: active denervation and chronic reinnervation changes in distal lower extremity muscles (amplitude-predominant in distal nerves). Findings indicate a neuropathy with terminal slowing as the predominant electrophysiological feature, distinct from uniform demyelination or pure axonal loss

csf.interpretation: Albuminocytologic dissociation: elevated CSF protein with normal cell count. Pattern is consistent with a demyelinating / paraproteinaemic neuropathy and helps distinguish anti-MAG / CIDP-spectrum from a pure axonal toxic neuropathy.

output.impression: Bone marrow biopsy: IgG kappa plasma cells <5% (residual myeloma in near-stringent CR — consistent with myeloma monitoring). ADDITIONALLY: small lymphoplasmacytic clone identified — IgM kappa lymphoplasmacytic cells comprising 3% of cellularity. Negative for Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia (lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma) — <10% threshold not met.

results.citation: Léger JM et al. (2013) Intravenous immunoglobulin versus placebo for anti-MAG neuropathy. Cochrane Database Syst Rev.
results.summary: IVIG is NOT recommended for anti-MAG neuropathy — trials show no significant benefit. Rituximab (anti-CD20) is the preferred treatment targeting the IgM-producing B cell clone. Response rate: ~50% partial improvement with rituximab 375 mg/m² x 4 weekly doses.

results.citation: Dalakas MC (2010) Advances in the diagnosis, pathogenesis and treatment of CIDP. Nat Rev Neurol 6:314-324.
results.summary: Anti-MAG neuropathy is distinguished from CIDP by: terminal slowing on NCS (DML disproportionately prolonged vs velocity), IgM paraprotein, anti-MAG antibody; CIDP responds to IVIG/steroids; anti-MAG does not respond to IVIG and requires rituximab.

output.impression: Sural nerve biopsy: widely spaced myelin lamellae on EM, with IgM and complement deposits on immunofluorescence at the myelin sheath. Findings indicate an antibody-mediated demyelinating process; serologic and clinical correlation recommended.

Anti-MAG Follow-up After Rituximab Cours.value: Neuropathic pain improved to 4/10 (from 8/10). Foot drop unchanged (axonal component). No further episodic grip weakness episodes.

Foot drop unchanged (axonal component). No further episodic grip weakness episodes. (H).

IVIG Safety Assessment (for educational.value: IVIG NOT indicated for anti-MAG neuropathy. Anti-MAG neuropathy is IVIG-refractory. Rituximab is the correct treatment.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Anti-MAG (IgM MGUS) demyelinating peripheral neuropathy with superimposed bortezomib-induced axonal neuropathy

differential.key_features: Predominantly painful sensory axonal; can persist; differentiates from anti-MAG by axonal-only pattern, normal SPEP/IFE, and no MAG antibody.
Demyelinating pattern with proximal involvement; need CSF and electrodiagnostic distinction (CIDP has conduction block; anti-MAG has terminal slowing).

differential.diagnosis: Myeloma relapse with peripheral nerve infiltration
differential.key_features: Re-stage with SPEP/IFE/light chains, bone marrow; cranial nerve involvement and gammopathy progression are red flags.
HbA1c 7.4% can contribute axonally but does not explain demyelinating pattern.
Painful small-fiber + autonomic + cardiac amyloidosis; fat-pad or nerve biopsy for Congo red.

optimal_actions.action: Order broad neuropathy labs (CBC, CMP, HbA1c, B12 + MMA, TSH, SPEP/IFE, urinalysis)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.action: Order EMG/NCS to characterize axonal vs demyelinating pattern and distribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.action: Search literature for DSP evaluation guidelines and etiology-specific recommendations
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.action: Review medications for neurotoxic agents and check interactions for symptomatic therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: SPEP / IFE / serum free light chains and anti-MAG antibody titer
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IgM monoclonal protein + high-titer anti-MAG IgM (Bühlmann ≥10,000 BTU) supports anti-MAG neuropathy

optimal_actions.action: Lumbar puncture for CSF when CIDP suspected
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Albuminocytologic dissociation (elevated protein, normal cell count) supports CIDP

optimal_actions.action: Bone marrow biopsy / hematology evaluation to distinguish MGUS, Waldenström's, and myeloma
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm IgM MGUS vs Waldenström's vs myeloma in setting of biclonal gammopathy with treated IgG kappa myeloma

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.

critical_actions: Recognize that demyelinating + terminal-slowing pattern and IgM paraprotein point to anti-MAG neuropathy
Send SPEP / IFE / serum free light chains and anti-MAG antibody titer
Address potential bortezomib-induced axonal component separately (dose reduction / discontinuation if ongoing)
Hematology re-evaluation for biclonal gammopathy and re-staging of myeloma
Consider rituximab (anti-MAG first-line) once IgM monoclonal protein and anti-MAG positivity are confirmed
contraindicated_actions: Do not attribute everything to bortezomib without addressing the demyelinating pattern and possible IgM paraprotein
Do not start IVIG as first-line for anti-MAG (typically poor response); rituximab is first-line
key_reasoning_points: Mixed demyelinating + axonal pattern with terminal slowing favors paraprotein-related demyelinating neuropathy
Anti-MAG neuropathy is distinct from CIDP: IgM paraprotein, terminal slowing, partial response to rituximab
Bortezomib is associated with painful axonal small-fiber neuropathy; usually improves on discontinuation

red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor entire picture on bortezomib toxicity
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Bortezomib causes axonal small-fiber neuropathy; demyelinating + terminal-slowing pattern is not bortezomib-typical and warrants anti-MAG workup.
